proposals.title: Fix CanonicalEncoder: captured trusted intrinsics and restricted container traversal
proposals.why_now: TASK-0004 has been attempted twice and rejected both times. Review-02 left two BLOCKER findings with explicit required changes. Until this passes review, StateHash cannot exist, and all downstream FASE-1 work — RNG, branded types, ledger, price generator, replay CLI, performance baseline — remains blocked. The required changes are narrow and well-specified by the reviewer: capture all built-in intrinsics at module initialization in frozen private bindings, and restrict container traversal to descriptor-based value reads using only those captured intrinsics so no user-controlled code (Proxy traps, overridden Set iterators, array index accessors) can execute or throw non-canonical errors.

proposals.title: Electron secure scaffolding, simulation worker IPC contract, and minimal FASE-1 installer
proposals.why_now: Section 14.6 contains a locked sequencing requirement: the installer must exist in FASE-1 in minimal form. The spec warns explicitly that deferring Electron bootstrap causes ABI and native-module problems to surface too late to fix architecture. INV-29 (contextIsolation, nodeIntegration:false, sandbox:true) is a named FASE-1 acceptance criterion. This track has no dependency on packages/core and can proceed in parallel with the encoder fix, reducing the total FASE-1 timeline. It has been proposed before but never assigned a task.

repository_assessment.current_state: TASK-0002 (npm workspaces monorepo bootstrap) is the only accepted task (checkpoint-0007). All 16 mandated workspace directories exist; strict TypeScript compilation, ESLint determinism rules, dependency boundary checker, and CI are in place. Every package source is a stub export {}. No ADRs exist in docs/decisions/. CanonicalEncoder (targeted by TASK-0003 and TASK-0004) has been attempted twice and rejected both times on REQUEST_CHANGES; checkpoint-0013 records NO_ACCEPTED_CHANGES. Review-02 on TASK-0004 attempt-02 identified two BLOCKER findings: container traversal can invoke user-controlled code (Proxy traps, overridden Set iterators, array index accessors), and encoder reads mutable global built-ins at call time rather than capturing them at module initialization.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: The CanonicalEncoder has two open BLOCKER findings from review-02 with explicit required changes. The spec mandates ADR-009 and the encoder be accepted before any StateHash implementation, which in turn blocks the replay CLI, the CI hash-comparison gate, and all FASE-1 invariant tests that depend on state hashing. In parallel, the Electron installer is a locked sequencing requirement (§14.6) that has never been assigned a task and can proceed independently of the encoder fix.

warnings: TASK-0004 has had two rejected implementations with structurally similar root causes (user-reachable code paths and mutable globals). The third implementation attempt must directly adopt the trusted-intrinsic capture pattern used by security-hardened serializers rather than making incremental fixes to the existing structure.

ADR-004 enforcement mechanism (DEFINIR) must be resolved before any bigint division is written in packages/domain. If lint-based enforcement is chosen, the lint rule must be active and blocking in CI before domain arithmetic code is introduced.

The transcendental-function prohibition in §13 combined with log-space price construction means the fixed-point or lookup-table ADR must be committed before packages/world emits any price values; implementing without it would embed unregistered approximation choices that cannot be changed without invalidating the hash.

tools/bench calibration ratios must be frozen in FASE-1 per the §18 baseline protocol, but cannot be frozen until packages/world price generation exists; this sequential dependency must not be deferred past FASE-1 acceptance.
